message.content:
I returned no link for e3 because I treated it as a report about a separate design, not as a statement about the Kyber rack architecture named by the open questions.

**What was shown:** e3 says SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia scrapped a planned **NVL72x2** design that would have put two **Oberon** racks back to back. It does not itself say that NVL72x2 was Kyber NVL144, part of Kyber’s rollout, or a cause of Kyber’s delay.

**Instructions I relied on:**  
- “File each statement under the narrowest question that names its matter, and under that one only; never add a broader question beside it.”  
- “News about a customer, supplier, competitor, product, policy or deal is filed under the question that names that matter … or under none when no question names it.”  
- “A rumour is filed exactly as a confirmed statement is.”

The closest questions were **v11**, which names the Kyber NVL144 rack architecture and its development and launch timing, and **v13**, which names the Kyber rack architecture and its launch by 2028. **What I inferred—and rejected—**was that the NVL72x2 cancellation might be part of the same Kyber rollout because it appeared in the same report or surrounding story. I did not treat that contextual association as enough to establish that e3 concerned the matter named by either question.

So the no-link placement reflects a strict reading of the statement, not proof that NVL72x2 had no connection to Kyber. If the source explicitly connected the scrapped design to Kyber’s development or launch, v11 or v13 could be appropriate; that connection was not present in e3’s text.
